title: The reciprocity rule: how a $1.99 Coke saved $400 on a Craigslist motorcycle
summary: A 2014 Sam Parr essay on using the reciprocity rule in negotiation. Give a small, unrequested gift before you ask for something, and the other person feels indebted. He shows it with a Coke on a motorcycle deal, a free speaking slot, and tipping and donation data.

principles.text: If you want something from someone, do them a favor or give a gift first, even an unrequested one.
principles.quote: If you want something from someone, do them a favor or give them a gift first…even if they don’t ask for it.

principles.text: Gifts work especially well on counterparties braced for a fight, because kindness catches them off guard.
principles.quote: Sellers are ready to go to war. They anticipate lowballers, tire-kickers, and flakes…so when a prospective buyer does something nice for you, even if it’s as small as smile and give you a Coke, you’re completely caught off guard with the kindness.

principles.text: Judge cheap tactics by expected value; a small cost is worth it if it even modestly raises your odds.
principles.quote: I’m willing to give a $1.99 gift even if it only increases the chances by 30%.

principles.text: Use gifts to land high-value asks: a thoughtful gift plus a handwritten note got a popular speaker to waive his fee.
principles.quote: I landed Andrew Warner, a popular internet personality, to speak at my conference for free by first giving him a bottle of scotch and a handwritten letter as a gift and then asking if he’d speak.

principles.text: Reciprocity is measurable: candy with the bill raised tips, and a delayed second piece raised them most.
principles.quote: Waiters who give a piece of candy with the bill get 3.3% larger tips. Waiters who give two pieces of candy get 14.1% larger tips. Waiters who delayed the action of giving the second piece of candy, for emphasis, raised tips by 23%.

principles.text: Give for real reasons, not just as manipulation; gift giving is good regardless of what you get back.
principles.quote: Gift giving is GOOD…regardless if you get something from it or not. Don’t use this powerful tool to become an evil genius.
